chunks: Abu Ghalib al-Zurari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding the Day of Doubt, whoever fasts it, he must make it up, and even if it is so. He means: whoever fasts it on the assumption that it is from the month of Ramadan without [definitive] sight [of the moon], he must make it up, even if it turns out to be a day from the month of Ramadan, because the Sunnah has come regarding its fasting on the assumption that it is from Sha'ban, and whoever contradicts it, he is obliged to make it up.

key_terms.قَضَاهُ: He makes it up / performs make-up fast

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for fasting on the Day of Doubt if one intends it is Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential nuance of the 'Day of Doubt' (Yawm al-Shakk), establishing that fasting with the intention of Ramadan without definitive proof requires a make-up fast (qada) even if it coincides with Ramadan. The ruling emphasizes adherence to the established Sunnah of treating the day as Sha'ban unless confirmed otherwise, reflecting the Shia scholarly preference for caution in distinguishing between obligatory and voluntary fasting. This principle underscores the importance of intention (niyyah) and certainty in ritual observance within the Twelver tradition.
